   853→	state, err = s.initializeSession(repo, sessionID, agentType, transcriptPath)
   854→	if err != nil {
   855→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to initialize session: %w", err)
   856→	}
   857→
   858→	// Calculate attribution for pre-prompt edits
   859→	// This captures any user edits made before the first prompt
   860→	promptAttr := s.calculatePromptAttributionAtStart(repo, state)
   861→	state.PendingPromptAttribution = &promptAttr
   862→	if err = s.saveSessionState(state); err != nil {
   863→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to save attribution: %w", err)
   864→	}

   867→	return nil
   868→}
   869→
   870→// calculatePromptAttributionAtStart calculates attribution at prompt start (before agent runs).
   871→// This captures user changes since the last checkpoint - no filtering needed since
   872→// the agent hasn't made any changes yet.
   873→//
   874→// IMPORTANT: This reads from the worktree (not staging area) to match what WriteTemporary
   875→// captures in checkpoints. If we read staged content but checkpoints capture worktree content,
   876→// unstaged changes would be in the checkpoint but not counted in PromptAttribution, causing
   877→// them to be incorrectly attributed to the agent later.
   878→func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) calculatePromptAttributionAtStart(
   879→	repo *git.Repository,
   880→	state *SessionState,
   881→) PromptAttribution {
   882→	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(context.Background(), "attribution")
   883→	nextCheckpointNum := state.CheckpointCount + 1
   884→	result := PromptAttribution{CheckpointNumber: nextCheckpointNum}
   885→
   886→	// Get last checkpoint tree from shadow branch (if it exists)
   887→	// For the first checkpoint, no shadow branch exists yet - this is fine,
   888→	// CalculatePromptAttribution will use baseTree as the reference instead.
   889→	var lastCheckpointTree *object.Tree
   890→	shadowBranchName := checkpoint.ShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
   891→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
   892→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
   893→	if err != nil {
   894→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: no shadow branch yet (first checkpoint)",
   895→			slog.String("shadow_branch", shadowBranchName))
   896→		// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
   897→	} else {
   898→		shadowCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
   899→		if err != nil {
   900→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: failed to get shadow commit",
   901→				slog.String("shadow_ref", ref.Hash().String()),
   902→				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   903→			// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
   904→		} else {
   905→			lastCheckpointTree, err = shadowCommit.Tree()
   906→			if err != nil {
   907→				logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: failed to get shadow tree",
   908→					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   909→				// Continue with lastCheckpointTree = nil
   910→			}
   911→		}
   912→	}
   913→
   914→	// Get base tree for agent lines calculation
   915→	var baseTree *object.Tree
   916→	if baseCommit, err := repo.CommitObject(plumbing.NewHash(state.BaseCommit)); err == nil {
   917→		if tree, treeErr := baseCommit.Tree(); treeErr == nil {
   918→			baseTree = tree
   919→		} else {
   920→			logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: base tree unavailable",
   921→				slog.String("error", treeErr.Error()))
   922→		}
   923→	} else {
   924→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution: base commit unavailable",
   925→			slog.String("base_commit", state.BaseCommit),
   926→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   927→	}
   928→
   929→	// Get worktree status to find ALL changed files
   930→	// Uses git CLI shim to avoid go-git index corruption (ENT-242).
   931→	status, err := gitutil.WorktreeStatus(repo)
   932→	if err != nil {
   933→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution skipped: failed to get worktree status",
   934→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   935→		return result
   936→	}
   937→
   938→	worktreeRoot, err := GetWorktreePath()
   939→	if err != nil {
   940→		logging.Debug(logCtx, "prompt attribution skipped: failed to get worktree path",
   941→			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
   942→		return result
   943→	}
   944→
   945→	// Build map of changed files with their worktree content
   946→	// IMPORTANT: We read from worktree (not staging area) to match what WriteTemporary
   947→	// captures in checkpoints. This ensures attribution is consistent.
   948→	changedFiles := make(map[string]string)
   949→	for filePath, fileStatus := range status {
   950→		// Skip unmodified files
   951→		if fileStatus.Worktree == git.Unmodified && fileStatus.Staging == git.Unmodified {
   952→			continue
   953→		}
   954→		// Skip .entire metadata directory (session data, not user code)
   955→		if strings.HasPrefix(filePath, paths.EntireMetadataDir+"/") || strings.HasPrefix(filePath, ".entire/") {
   956→			continue
   957→		}
   958→
   959→		// Always read from worktree to match checkpoint behavior
   960→		fullPath := filepath.Join(worktreeRoot, filePath)
   961→		var content string
   962→		if data, err := os.ReadFile(fullPath); err == nil { //nolint:gosec // filePath is from git worktree status
   963→			// Use git's binary detection algorithm (matches getFileContent behavior).
   964→			// Binary files are excluded from line-based attribution calculations.
   965→			isBinary, binErr := binary.IsBinary(bytes.NewReader(data))
   966→			if binErr == nil && !isBinary {
   967→				content = string(data)
   968→			}
   969→		}
   970→		// else: file deleted, unreadable, or binary - content remains empty string
   971→
   972→		changedFiles[filePath] = content
   973→	}
   974→
   975→	// Use CalculatePromptAttribution from manual_commit_attribution.go
   976→	result = CalculatePromptAttribution(baseTree, lastCheckpointTree, changedFiles, nextCheckpointNum)
   977→
   978→	return result
   979→}

1→// Package gitutil provides git CLI shims that return go-git types.
     2→//
     3→// go-git v5's worktree.Status() reads and rewrites the index file.
     4→// When called from git hook paths (post-commit, prepare-commit-msg),
     5→// this can corrupt the index by writing stale cache-tree entries that
     6→// reference objects pruned by GC. These shims use git CLI instead,
     7→// which reads the index without rewriting it.
     8→//
     9→// See ENT-242 for details. When go-git v6 fixes index corruption,
    10→// the shim functions can be swapped back to native go-git calls.
    11→package gitutil
    12→
    13→import (
    14→	"bytes"
    15→	"context"
    16→	"fmt"
    17→	"os/exec"
    18→	"strings"
    19→
    20→	"github.com/go-git/go-git/v5"
    21→)
    22→
    23→// WorktreeStatus returns the worktree status using git CLI instead of go-git.
    24→//
    25→// Parses `git status --porcelain -z` (NUL-delimited, handles special chars)
    26→// and returns the same git.Status type for drop-in compatibility with
    27→// callers that previously used worktree.Status().
    28→//
    29→// Uses -uall to list individual untracked files instead of collapsing
    30→// directories, matching go-git's worktree.Status() behavior.
    31→//
    32→// When go-git v6 fixes index corruption (ENT-242), swap to:
    33→//
    34→//	w, _ := repo.Worktree(); return w.Status()
    35→func WorktreeStatus(repo *git.Repository) (git.Status, error) {
    36→	output, err := runGitCmd(repo, "git status", "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "-uall")
    37→	if err != nil {
    38→		return nil, err
    39→	}
    40→	return parsePorcelainStatus(string(output)), nil
    41→}
    42→
    43→// StagedFileNames returns just the names of files staged for commit.
    44→// Uses `git diff --cached --name-only -z` which is lighter than a full status.
    45→//
    46→// When go-git v6 fixes index corruption (ENT-242), swap to:
    47→//
    48→//	w, _ := repo.Worktree(); s, _ := w.Status(); filter for Staging != Unmodified
    49→func StagedFileNames(repo *git.Repository) ([]string, error) {
    50→	output, err := runGitCmd(repo, "git diff --cached", "diff", "--cached", "--name-only", "-z")
    51→	if err != nil {
    52→		return nil, err
    53→	}
    54→	return parseNulDelimitedNames(string(output)), nil
    55→}
    56→
    57→// runGitCmd runs a git command in the worktree root, capturing stderr for
    58→// diagnostics on failure.
    59→func runGitCmd(repo *git.Repository, label string, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
    60→	repoRoot, err := worktreeRoot(repo)
    61→	if err != nil {
    62→		return nil, err
    63→	}
    64→
    65→	cmd := exec.CommandContext(context.Background(), "git", args...)
    66→	cmd.Dir = repoRoot
    67→	var stderr bytes.Buffer
    68→	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
    69→	output, err := cmd.Output()
    70→	if err != nil {
    71→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s failed in %s: %w: %s", label, repoRoot, err, strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String()))
    72→	}
    73→	return output, nil
    74→}
    75→
    76→// worktreeRoot returns the filesystem root of the repo's worktree.
    77→func worktreeRoot(repo *git.Repository) (string, error) {
    78→	wt, err := repo.Worktree()
    79→	if err != nil {
    80→		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree: %w", err)
    81→	}
    82→	return wt.Filesystem.Root(), nil
    83→}
    84→
    85→// parseNulDelimitedNames splits NUL-delimited output into a string slice,
    86→// dropping empty elements (e.g., trailing NUL).
    87→func parseNulDelimitedNames(raw string) []string {
    88→	if raw == "" {
    89→		return nil
    90→	}
    91→	parts := strings.Split(raw, "\x00")
    92→	var names []string
    93→	for _, p := range parts {
    94→		if p != "" {
    95→			names = append(names, p)
    96→		}
    97→	}
    98→	return names
    99→}

   101→// porcelainStatusCode maps a single byte from `git status --porcelain` XY output
   102→// to the corresponding go-git StatusCode.
   103→func porcelainStatusCode(b byte) git.StatusCode {
   104→	switch b {
   105→	case ' ':
   106→		return git.Unmodified
   107→	case 'M':
   108→		return git.Modified
   109→	case 'T':
   110→		// Type change — go-git has no dedicated code; treat as Modified.
   111→		return git.Modified
   112→	case 'A':
   113→		return git.Added
   114→	case 'D':
   115→		return git.Deleted
   116→	case 'R':
   117→		return git.Renamed
   118→	case 'C':
   119→		return git.Copied
   120→	case '?':
   121→		return git.Untracked
   122→	case '!':
   123→		// Ignored — callers typically skip these; map to Untracked so they
   124→		// are visible rather than silently dropped.
   125→		return git.Untracked
   126→	case 'U':
   127→		return git.UpdatedButUnmerged
   128→	default:
   129→		return git.Unmodified
   130→	}
   131→}
   132→
   133→// parsePorcelainStatus parses NUL-delimited `git status --porcelain -z` output
   134→// into a git.Status map. The format is:
   135→//
   136→//	XY filename\0            — for most entries
   137→//	XY newname\0oldname\0    — for renames (R) and copies (C)
   138→func parsePorcelainStatus(raw string) git.Status {
   139→	status := make(git.Status)
   140→	if raw == "" {
   141→		return status
   142→	}
   143→
   144→	entries := strings.Split(raw, "\x00")
   145→	for i := 0; i < len(entries); i++ {
   146→		entry := entries[i]
   147→		if len(entry) < 3 {
   148→			continue // trailing empty element or malformed
   149→		}
   150→
   151→		x := entry[0] // staging status
   152→		y := entry[1] // worktree status
   153→		filename := entry[3:]
   154→
   155→		fs := &git.FileStatus{
   156→			Staging:  porcelainStatusCode(x),
   157→			Worktree: porcelainStatusCode(y),
   158→		}
   159→
   160→		// Renames and copies have a second NUL-separated entry (the old name).
   161→		// Check both X (staging) and Y (worktree) columns defensively.
   162→		if x == 'R' || x == 'C' || y == 'R' || y == 'C' {
   163→			if i+1 < len(entries) && entries[i+1] != "" {
   164→				fs.Extra = entries[i+1]
   165→				i++ // skip old-name entry
   166→			}
   167→		}
   168→
   169→		status[filename] = fs
   170→	}
   171→
   172→	return status
   173→}

   182→// commitCodeResult contains the result of committing code to the active branch.
   183→type commitCodeResult struct {
   184→	CommitHash plumbing.Hash
   185→	Created    bool // True if a new commit was created, false if skipped (no changes)
   186→}
   187→
   188→// commitCodeToActive commits code changes to the active branch.
   189→// Adds an Entire-Checkpoint trailer for metadata lookup that survives amend/rebase.
   190→// Returns the result containing commit hash and whether a commit was created.
   191→func (s *AutoCommitStrategy) commitCodeToActive(repo *git.Repository, ctx SaveContext, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (commitCodeResult, error) {
   192→	// Check if there are any code changes to commit
   193→	if len(ctx.ModifiedFiles) == 0 && len(ctx.NewFiles) == 0 && len(ctx.DeletedFiles) == 0 {
   194→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "No code changes to commit to active branch\n")
   195→		// Return current HEAD hash but mark as not created
   196→		head, err := repo.Head()
   197→		if err != nil {
   198→			return commitCodeResult{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD: %w", err)
   199→		}
   200→		return commitCodeResult{CommitHash: head.Hash(), Created: false}, nil
   201→	}
   202→
   203→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
   204→	if err != nil {
   205→		return commitCodeResult{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to get worktree: %w", err)
   206→	}
   207→
   208→	// Get HEAD hash before commit to detect if commitOrHead actually creates a new commit
   209→	// (commitOrHead returns HEAD hash without error when git.ErrEmptyCommit occurs)
   210→	headBefore, err := repo.Head()
   211→	if err != nil {
   212→		return commitCodeResult{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to get HEAD: %w", err)
   213→	}
   214→
   215→	// Stage code changes
   216→	StageFiles(worktree, ctx.ModifiedFiles, ctx.NewFiles, ctx.DeletedFiles, StageForSession)
   217→

   219→	commitMsg := ctx.CommitMessage + "\n\n" + trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey + ": " + checkpointID.String()
   220→
   221→	author := &object.Signature{
   222→		Name:  ctx.AuthorName,
   223→		Email: ctx.AuthorEmail,
   224→		When:  time.Now(),
   225→	}
   226→	commitHash, err := commitOrHead(repo, worktree, commitMsg, author)
   227→	if err != nil {
   228→		return commitCodeResult{}, err
   229→	}
   230→

   232→	created := commitHash != headBefore.Hash()
   233→	if created {
   234→		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Committed code changes to active branch (%s)\n", commitHash.String()[:7])
   235→	}

   240→// Metadata is stored at sharded path: <checkpointID[:2]>/<checkpointID[2:]>/
   241→// This allows direct lookup from the checkpoint ID trailer on the code commit.
   242→// Uses checkpoint.WriteCommitted for git operations.
   243→func (s *AutoCommitStrategy) commitMetadataToMetadataBranch(repo *git.Repository, ctx SaveContext, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
   244→	store, err := s.getCheckpointStore()

   257→

   260→		CheckpointID:                checkpointID,
   261→		SessionID:                   sessionID,
   262→		Strategy:                    StrategyNameAutoCommit, // Use new strategy name
   263→		Branch:                      branchName,
   264→		MetadataDir:                 ctx.MetadataDirAbs, // Copy all files from metadata dir
   265→		AuthorName:                  ctx.AuthorName,
   266→		AuthorEmail:                 ctx.AuthorEmail,
   267→		Agent:                       ctx.AgentType,
   268→		TranscriptIdentifierAtStart: ctx.TranscriptIdentifierAtStart,
   269→		TranscriptLinesAtStart:      ctx.TranscriptLinesAtStart,
   270→		TokenUsage:                  ctx.TokenUsage,
   271→		CheckpointsCount:            1,            // Each auto-commit checkpoint = 1
   272→		FilesTouched:                filesTouched, // Track modified files (same as manual-commit)
   273→	})
